_note_injection: Data-driven, set 2026-09-01 after retraining the head with ~344 benign 'hard-negative' rows (report/audit/SAST/CVE-detail/pentest phrasing loaded with trigger words; scripts/build_sanitize_dataset.py HN_* families) — the InjecGuard 'Mitigating Over-defense' idea done with templates. Chosen from a threshold sweep on the HELD-OUT sets evals/sanitize/{overdefense,attacks}.jsonl (see scripts/eval_sanitize.py): the retrained head's minimum true-attack injection score is 0.398, and benign hard-negative scores dropped ~half vs the shipped head (audit-imperative mean 0.344->0.161, kpi-known-fp mean 0.277->0.104). At 0.35 the head keeps injection recall 36/36=100% (baseline shipped head at 0.6 was 34/36=94.4%, missing 2 tool-abuse) while over-defense false positives fall to 6/211=2.8% (baseline 8/211=3.8% at 0.6) — strictly better on BOTH axes, and all 11 real KPI-bench false positives PASS. This REPLACES the 0.6 stopgap (was a mitigation, not a fix). Residual FP is confined to the hardest imperative 'find every SQLi/XSS/RCE and how it's exploited' audit phrasings (scores 0.40-0.67); closing those needs more targeted hard-negatives (tracked in docs/input-classifier-improvement-plan.md). Retrain offline via: HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python scripts/train_sanitize_head.py --embed st --model DuyTa/sec-embedding --head mixed
